title: Butterfly Operation Visualizer
description: An interactive butterfly with editable complex inputs and a selectable twiddle factor, showing the four-multiply complex product and how one shared W*b feeds both outputs.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
FFT
Algorithms

learningObjectives: Calculate both butterfly outputs from chosen inputs and twiddle factor
Demonstrate that both outputs share a single product
Expand a complex multiply into four real multiplies
prerequisites: Twiddle factors on the unit circle

controls.label: Compute
controls.purpose: Animate the shared product travelling to both outputs

equations: (w_re + w_im i)(b_re + b_im i) = (w_re b_re - w_im b_im) + (w_re b_im + w_im b_re) i
assumptions: Twiddle factors drawn from an 8-point transform
Exact floating-point arithmetic; fixed-point effects are covered separately
limitations: Shows one butterfly in isolation; stage assembly and bit-reversal ordering appear in later sims

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Apply-level calculator with a data-flow visualization
keyQuestions: How many real multiplies does one complex multiply require?
Which twiddle values need no general multiply at all?
commonMisconceptions: That each butterfly output needs its own twiddle multiply
That a complex multiply is a single machine operation
assessmentOpportunities: Count the complex multiplies saved by sharing across 512 butterflies
